name: Orbit AI - Phase 4 - Churn risk win-back (new, not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Every Monday at 7am
nodes.notes: 06's audit-gap list: 'churn/win-back.' No timing or trigger rule is given anywhere in the source docs for this one (unlike CX cadence's brief-given 7/30/60/90-day numbers) - weekly, not daily, is this pass's own judgment call: engagementScore (health-scoring.workflow.json, itself already a judgment-call formula) only recomputes once a day and moves slowly, so checking more often than weekly would mostly re-examine unchanged scores. Runs after health-scoring.workflow.json (6am daily) so today's score is always current by the time this reads it.

nodes.name: Fetch LiveClient Companies
nodes.notes: Same query cx-cadence.workflow.json and health-scoring.workflow.json both use - post-sale, Company not Opportunity, same load-bearing distinction every post-sale automation in this repo follows.

nodes.name: Draft win-back message

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-opus-5', max_tokens: 512, system: [{ type: 'text', text: 'You draft short, warm retention/win-back check-ins for an existing client whose engagement appears to have dropped. Never mention a numeric score or that they were flagged by an algorithm - frame it as a genuine account-rep check-in ('wanted to see how things are going', ask what could be better, offer to hop on a call). No guilt, no pressure, no hint that the relationship is at risk. DRAFT ONLY for the account rep to review before sending - never implies it has been sent.', cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } }], messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Company: ' + $json.name + '
Client since: ' + $json.liveClientSince + '
Win-back attempt: ' + $json.winbackAttempt + '
Draft a retention check-in.' }] }) }}

nodes.notes: Draft only - a churn win-back touch is an external send like every nurture/CX draft in this repo, human approves/sends, same automation risk boundary. The system prompt explicitly forbids exposing the score/algorithm to the client - the client should experience this as a person checking in, not a system flagging them.

nodes.name: Update Company churn state

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ churnWinbackSentAt: new Date().toISOString(), churnWinbackAttemptCount: $('Decide at-risk clients').item.json.winbackAttempt, churnWinbackDraftText: $json.draftText }) }}

nodes.notes: Advances regardless of whether the rep actually sends the draft, same reasoning as nurture-cadence.workflow.json and cx-cadence.workflow.json's own state-write nodes - churnWinbackSentAt being set is what starts this company's COOLDOWN_DAYS window, not the rep's send action, since this workflow has no way to observe whether a send actually happened.

nodes.name: Alert: churn risk win-back ready

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'warning', source: 'churn-winback', message: $('Decide at-risk clients').item.json.name + ' is showing low engagement (score ' + $('Decide at-risk clients').item.json.engagementScore + ') - win-back draft ready (attempt ' + $('Decide at-risk clients').item.json.winbackAttempt + ').', linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/company/' + $('Decide at-risk clients').item.json.id }) }}

nodes.notes: Routes to #cx-retention (alertRouting.ts's cx-retention route already matches 'churn'). severity:'warning', not 'info' like the routine nurture/CX drafts - a client trending toward churn deserves more visibility than a routine scheduled touch.
